verdict.rationale: The evidence shows no documented feature for issuing scoped, least-privilege API credentials to an agent, such as scoped API keys or agent or service tokens. What it does show are developer building blocks: user JWTs that RLS policies can scope row by row, a Custom Access Token Hook that changes claims, self-signed JWTs from an imported signing key, and a configurable JWT expiry. A developer could assemble agent credentials from these, but they are not the capability itself, so they earn no credit.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent
